pr_title: Move timeline by one step when sprite frame track is created

issue_context.title: Animation editor timeline playhead does not advance when adding a key if the confirmation dialog appears
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
3.2 beta 1 mono

**OS/device including version:**
Win10 Home 64

**Issue description:**
It can be seen that when you enter the first frame by clicking on the key icon to add a keyframe, the frame is entered in the animation editor but the timeline did not move, then when you click on the key icon again , the second frame overlaps the first frame.
The first frame disappears, it cannot be selected.
Although you double clicked on the key icon, only the second frame was added.
The first frame was overwritten.

**_The problem was that the timeline did not shift when the first frame was introduced._**

I would like to add something, add a new animation by pressing the "Animation" -> "New" button should bring the timeline to 0.

**Steps to reproduce:**
Add the initial keyframe in the animation editor and then a new keyframe.

The first frame will be overwritten by the second frame, then even though you pressed the keyframe add button twice, only the second frame was added to the animation editor.

![GIF](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/19652075/69012103-45314500-0972-11ea-9689-dc2fe8c9dfa1.gif)

**Minimal reproduction project:**
[animationEditorBug.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/3855960/animationEditorBug.zip)
comments:
The solution to this problem is to apply the rule that every time a frame is added to the timeline, the time bar must move automatically.
Currently that is not happening when the create framekey icon is pressed for the first time.

I believe this issue has existed since at least 2.1, probably even always.  Might even be an issue somewhere for it...

The work around we've used is to click the keyframe and then scrub the timeline forward then backward, re-keyframe over top the first, and then it will advance.

Seems it doesn't want to advance a step if there is no existing keyframes.

There really are two possible and valid paths.

On the initial press of the "Add keyframe" button the timeline of the animation is created, then two things can happen afterwards:

A - If the editor inserts a new frame automatically, then the line should move automatically.

B - If the editor does not insert any frame automatically, then the line should not be moved, leaving 0.0 ready to add the first animation frame. Thus, the first press of the "Add keyframe" button would have served only to create the timeline of the animation. Now a new press on the button will add the animation frame.

** You should also keep in mind that this property (of the sprite node) should not be altered (it should not advance) if a new animation frame is not added (this would be in option B).
![1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/19652075/69276347-99d8f800-0bde-11ea-8030-bc525c6c249b.png)
uhf that's awkward. Note to self: "don't include issue id when trying to something in git you haven't done before" :D
Ok it's not fixed if you have confirmation enabled. It's only correct when you insert without confirmation.

I think this bug exist since 3.1 at least and still exists in Godot 3.2.3 stable, Godot 3.3 rc8

If the user presses the key sympol on a property without an existing track, after the first key is set, the timestamp is not advanced, therefore the first key is overwritten by the second key:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47016402/114317464-7fbbf480-9b08-11eb-9f70-b07f2baa308a.mp4

This is not just a problem with sprite frames (used here to make it more obvious), but any kind of property.
See simple steps to reproduce here:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/47808

Stay present at v3.5.beta1.official [b9b23d222]
When the first key is added, the animationplayer's timebar doesn't advance, however it does advance with any other keys added after the first one.

review_comments:
This kind of string comparison is likely to be unreliable, does it work if the Sprite is not named "Sprite"?

This is not the proper way to do this, you should instead rely on the `PROPERTY_USAGE_KEYING_INCREMENTS` usage flag which is assigned for this property, and which is used already in `editor_inspector.cpp` to enable the increment of the frame number on keying.

This logic should also be done earlier, here you're after `undo_redo->commit_action()`, so this breaks the undo/redo feature.

Thank you for the feedback this is my first time doing something like this sorry for the mistakes. 

I will try changing the things you mentioned. :)

No worry, you did a good job already finding a partial solution :)

You can look a bit further up in the section with the comment "// Hack.", I think you might need to do similar handling for this case (retrieving the property to get its usage flag, checking that it's `PROPERTY_USAGE_KEYING_INCREMENTS`, and if so increment the position by the timeline step).
